subject: SCI
title: Chemistry in the Earth System
description: The second course in California's three-course NGSS high school model, connecting chemistry to Earth's systems. Students investigate combustion, atomic structure and the origin of elements in stars, bonding and material properties, energy flow in the Earth system, reaction stoichiometry, the chemistry of climate change, reaction rates and equilibrium, and ocean acidification. Every week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials or a PhET simulation, plus data analysis and claim-evidence-reasoning writing.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (HS); 2016 CA Science Framework – Chemistry in the Earth System

standards.HS-PS1-1: Use the periodic table as a model to predict relative properties of elements based on outer-energy-level electrons.
standards.HS-PS1-2: Construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction based on atomic structure and periodic trends.
standards.HS-PS1-3: Plan and conduct an investigation to gather evidence to compare bulk-scale structure of substances to infer strength of electrical forces between particles.
standards.HS-PS1-4: Develop a model to illustrate that release or absorption of energy from a reaction depends on changes in total bond energy.
standards.HS-PS1-5: Apply scientific principles and evidence to explain effects of temperature and concentration on reaction rate.
standards.HS-PS1-6: Refine the design of a chemical system by specifying a change in conditions that would produce increased amounts of products at equilibrium.
standards.HS-PS1-7: Use mathematical representations to support the claim that atoms, and therefore mass, are conserved during a chemical reaction.
standards.HS-PS1-8: Develop models to illustrate changes in the composition of the nucleus and energy released during fission, fusion, and radioactive decay.
standards.HS-PS2-6: Communicate why molecular-level structure is important in the functioning of designed materials.
standards.HS-PS3-1: Create a computational model to calculate the change in energy of one component in a system when the change in energy of others is known.
standards.HS-PS3-2: Develop and use models to illustrate that energy at the macroscopic scale can be accounted for as motion of particles and energy stored in fields.
standards.HS-PS3-3: Design, build, and refine a device that converts one form of energy into another within constraints.
standards.HS-PS3-4: Plan and conduct an investigation to show that transfer of thermal energy in a closed system results in more uniform energy distribution (second law).
standards.HS-ESS1-1: Develop a model based on evidence to illustrate the life span of the Sun and the role of nuclear fusion in releasing energy that reaches Earth.
standards.HS-ESS1-3: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.
standards.HS-ESS2-2: Analyze geoscience data to make the claim that one change to Earth's surface can create feedbacks that cause changes to other Earth systems.
standards.HS-ESS2-3: Develop a model based on evidence of Earth's interior to describe the cycling of matter by thermal convection.
standards.HS-ESS2-4: Use a model to describe how variations in the flow of energy into and out of Earth's systems result in changes in climate.
standards.HS-ESS2-5: Plan and conduct an investigation of the properties of water and its effects on Earth materials and surface processes.
standards.HS-ESS2-6: Develop a quantitative model to describe the cycling of carbon among the hydrosphere, atmosphere, geosphere, and biosphere.
standards.HS-ESS3-4: Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
standards.HS-ESS3-5: Analyze geoscience data and results from global climate models to make an evidence-based forecast of the current rate of global or regional climate change.
standards.HS-ESS3-6: Use a computational representation to illustrate relationships among Earth systems and how those relationships are being modified by human activity.
standards.HS-ETS1-1: Analyze a major global challenge to specify qualitative and quantitative criteria and constraints for solutions.
standards.HS-ETS1-3: Evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs.

units.title: Combustion: Matter and Energy
units.big_idea: Burning fuel rearranges atoms and releases stored energy that powers society and changes the atmosphere.

units.title: Atoms, Elements and the Stars
units.big_idea: Every element on Earth was forged in stars; atomic structure explains periodic patterns.

units.title: Bonding, Structure and Materials
units.big_idea: Electrical forces between particles determine a substance's properties and uses.

units.title: Heat and Energy in the Earth System
units.big_idea: Thermal energy flows from hot to cold, driving Earth's interior convection and surface systems.

units.title: Chemical Reactions and Stoichiometry
units.big_idea: Atoms are conserved in reactions, so quantities can be predicted mathematically.

units.title: Chemistry of Climate Change
units.big_idea: Greenhouse gases alter Earth's energy balance; carbon cycles among spheres.

units.title: Reaction Rates and Equilibrium
units.big_idea: Collisions control reaction speed, and systems shift to counter changes.

units.title: Water, Acids and Ocean Acidification
units.big_idea: Water's unique properties shape Earth, and dissolved CO₂ is changing ocean chemistry.

units.title: Capstone and Final Assessment
units.big_idea: Chemistry explains and helps solve real environmental challenges.
